questions.question: Write a short note on special horticultural practices followed in greenhouse cultivation of Cucumber.
questions.solution_html:
• Special horticultural practices in cucumber include trellising for vertical growth, pruning
  • (removing lower side shoots/leaves), and using specific chemical sprays to influence flower sex

  • Heating system-unit heaters,centralized,infrared,solar

questions.question: List out the components of a typical greenhouse with a neat diagram.
Explain in brief:1. Unit heaters 2. Boiler.
questions.solution_html:
• A unit heater is a self-contained, non-ducted device that heats the specific area where it is
  • installed. It uses a fuel source (like natural gas, propane, or electricity) to heat a heat exchanger. A
  • powerful internal fan then blows air over that exchanger and directly into the room.
  • Boilers are the heart of a greenhouse's central heating system, typically chosen for larger
  • commercial operations (over 1,000 m²) or facilities requiring precise temperature control. Unlike
  • unit heaters that blow hot air, boilers use water or steam to transport heat, which is up to 3,500
  • times more efficient at carrying energy than air.
questions.final_answer: times more efficient at carrying energy than air

questions.question: Briefly describe the role of active winter cooling system in greenhouse.
questions.solution_html:
• Convection Tube Cooling: A fan introduces cold outside air into a plastic tube running along
  • the greenhouse ceiling, allowing the air to warm up slightly before it descends to the plant zone.
  • Horizontal Air Flow (HAF) Fans: Fans are positioned to move air horizontally along the length of
  • the greenhouse, blending cool air from vents with the existing warm air to prevent cold spots.
questions.final_answer: the greenhouse, blending cool air from vents with the existing warm air to prevent cold spots

questions.question: Role of microprocessors and computers in controlling environment inside a greenhouse.
questions.solution_html:
• Microprocessors and computers act as the "brain" of a modern greenhouse, transforming it into a
  • self-regulating ecosystem by continuously monitoring and adjusting environmental variables.
  • Sensors: Gather analog signals .
  • Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC): Converts sensor readings into a digital format the
  • microprocessor can process.
  • Microprocessor/Microcomputer: Executes programmed logic to decide whether to activate
  • or deactivate equipment.
  • Actuators & Relays: Physical components (fans, heaters, sprinklers) that carry out the
  • processor's commands.

questions.question: What are the different substrates used in protected cultivation?Discuss in detail
questions.solution_html:
• 1. Organic Substrates (Bio-based)
  •  Cocopeat : Derived from coconut husks; popular for its high water retention and
  • durability.
  •  Peat Moss: Decomposed plant matter with high moisture holding and acidity; excellent
  • for seedlings.
  •  Rice Hulls & Bark: Used primarily in mixes to improve drainage and reduce weight.
questions.final_answer:  Rice Hulls & Bark: Used primarily in mixes to improve drainage and reduce weight

questions.question: Discuss in detail about problem management in protected cultivation
questions.solution_html:
• Effective greenhouse problem management focuses on proactive sanitation, environmental
  • control, and Integrated Pest Management (IPM) to prevent, detect, and treat issues like pests, diseases
  • and equipment failures. Key strategies include cleaning, scouting, and using biological controls
  • supported by maintaining proper humidity and temperature to reduce pathogen growth.
  • Use treated root substrates.
